newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to pay miners, address non-payments.
newsitem.headline: Russia to pay miners, address non-payments.

text.p: The Russian government will begin to pay its own debts and work to help resolve non-payment crisis across the country, top officials said on Wednesday.

Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin promised Russia as a whole would pay 11.8 trillion roubles ($2.1 billion) in back wages and pensions in March and said the government would pay almost three trillion of that. It was not clear where the money would come from to meet arrears payments.
First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said that total non-payments in Russia were 53 trillion, which he called a "fantastic" sum.
A web of non-payments between government, industry and workers is considered a strong brake on the economy and one reason that trade unions have organised a national day of strikes on Thursday.
Chubais promised the government would clear its debt backlog to the mining industry, which is one of the worst off sectors in the economy, by paying 6.5 trillion roubles.
But Chernomyrdin said that tax collection, which is far below targeted levels, would be a major difficulty for Russia in March.
